name: S-400 Triumf (India)

header.one_liner: Russian long-range air defence system; India contracted 5 regiments for ~$5.4 billion in 2018; 3 delivered by 2024; deliveries delayed by Russia-Ukraine war.

at_a_glance.Range: Up to 400 km (40N6 missile); 250 km (48N6); 120 km (9M96E2); 40 km (9M96E)
at_a_glance.Altitude: Up to 30 km (40N6); 5 m to 30 km
at_a_glance.Missile_types: 4 missile types per battery: 40N6 (400 km), 48N6 (250 km), 9M96E2 (120 km), 9M96E (40 km)

what_it_is.prose: The S-400 Triumf (NATO reporting name SA-21 Growler) is a Russian long-range surface-to-air missile system developed by Almaz-Antey. India signed a $5.4 billion (₹40,000 crore) contract in October 2018 for five S-400 regiments, despite the threat of US Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (CAATSA) sanctions. Each S-400 regiment typically comprises a command post, surveillance radar, and 2-3 batteries with 4 launchers each, capable of firing four different missile types covering ranges from 40 km to 400 km: the 40N6 (400 km), 48N6 (250 km), 9M96E2 (120 km), and 9M96E (40 km). A single battery can simultaneously engage up to 36 targets (80 with a full regiment). As of 2024, three of the five contracted regiments have been delivered to the Indian Army's Air Defence Corps. The remaining two regiments are delayed due to the Russia-Ukraine war disrupting Russian defence exports. Reported deployment locations (not officially confirmed) include the Punjab sector (facing Pakistan and the western China border), the Rajasthan sector, and the Eastern sector. The S-400 provides India's outermost air defence layer, complementing the Indo-Israeli MRSAM (medium-range), the indigenous Akash/Akash-NG (medium-short), and QRSAM (short-range) systems. The CAATSA sanctions threat has not been invoked against India as of August 2026, though the US has periodically signaled concerns.

faq.question: How many S-400 regiments has India received, and how many are pending?
faq.answer: India contracted 5 S-400 regiments in October 2018 for approximately $5.4 billion (₹40,000 crore). Three regiments had been delivered by March 2024. The remaining two regiments are delayed due to the Russia-Ukraine war disrupting Russian defence exports. New delivery timelines have not been confirmed by Russia or the Indian MoD as of August 2026.

faq.question: Has the US invoked CAATSA sanctions against India for the S-400 deal?
faq.answer: No. The US Countering America's Adversaries Through Sanctions Act (CAATSA) threatens sanctions against countries purchasing Russian defence equipment, but the US has not invoked CAATSA against India as of August 2026. However, periodic US signals of concern continue, and the issue remains a point of friction in the India-US strategic relationship. India has consistently argued that the S-400 is essential for its national security and that CAATSA should not apply to a strategic partner.

faq.question: Where are the Indian S-400 systems deployed?
faq.answer: Deployment locations are not officially confirmed by the Indian MoD. However, credible reporting indicates three deployment sectors: the Punjab sector (facing Pakistan and the western China border), the Rajasthan sector, and the Eastern sector (facing China). The S-400 provides India's outermost air defence layer, complementing the Indo-Israeli MRSAM (medium-range), the indigenous Akash and Akash-NG (medium-short), and QRSAM (short-range) systems.
